title: Wireframe
body:
A **wireframe** is a layout drawing showing structure and hierarchy with the visual design
deliberately absent. Boxes stand for regions, lines stand for text, and no colours, fonts or
images appear.

```
+--------------------------------------+
|  [logo]              [nav] [nav]     |
+--------------------------------------+
|                                      |
|   ====== heading =========           |
|   ---------------------------        |
|   ---------------------------        |
|                                      |
|   [ primary action ]                 |
+--------------------------------------+
```

Leaving out the visual design is the technique. A stakeholder shown a polished mockup discusses
the colour, and one shown a wireframe discusses whether the primary action is findable, which
is the question at this stage.

Wireframes are the low-fidelity half of [[Prototyping]], and they answer what goes on the
screen, what is grouped with what, and what is most prominent. They cannot answer whether the
interaction feels right, which needs something interactive.
